clue.text: Head comes off optical instrument, but it's still going

indicators.note: the first letter of the instrument's name is lopped away, like a head coming off

parts.note: a sextant is a navigator's optical instrument for measuring angles

explanation.surface: A telescope-like device loses its top part yet somehow keeps working.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extant is still in existence, surviving rather than lost or extinct.

clue.text: When free, retire to a place abroad

indicators.note: setting the letters free lets them scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: Once released from work, someone retires to a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges RETIRE plus A; 'When' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a country in the Horn of Africa, a foreign place for a British solver.

clue.text: Project to cause confusion

definitions.meaning: to disconcert or fluster someone, as in a question that threw them

explanation.surface: A scheme meant to sow confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' looks like a noun (a scheme) but is the verb to hurl.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw is to project something forward, and also to disconcert someone.

clue.text: Unable to fix bearing of stars

indicators.note: fixing the letters means mending them into a new order

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A navigator cannot take a bearing from the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fix' rearranges UNABLE into NEBULA, then E for east is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebulae are clouds of gas and dust in space, some of them clusters of stars.

clue.text: Cannonball?

parts.note: read as a ball for a cannon: a light quick-firing gun named for its sound, and also a round woolly ball on a hat

explanation.surface: A one-word question about artillery ammunition.
explanation.walkthrough: The word splits into a type of automatic cannon (named for its firing noise) and a decorative fluffy ball; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a quick-firing automatic gun and a little woolly ball, so it is a cannon and a ball at once.

clue.text: Attacks aimed at badgers?

definitions.meaning: assaults, as in the onslaught of an enemy
a badger's burrow is a set (or sett), so this reads as 'directed at badgers' homes'

explanation.surface: Raids directed against badgers.
explanation.walkthrough: A badger's den is called a set or sett, so ON SETS is directed at badgers' homes.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an attack or assault, as well as a beginning.

clue.text: Eliminate European cricket side

parts.note: a Pole is Polish, from a European country
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: Knocking out a European cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the leg (on) side relative to the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish off is an idiom meaning to finish or dispose of something or someone completely.

clue.text: He produces a pass when charged

definitions.text: He produces a pass when charged

parts.words: He produces a pass when charged
parts.note: 'charged' sounds like a fee, but here a bull charges and the cape sweeps aside

explanation.surface: Someone who issues a permit once paid.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'pass' sounds like a ticket issued for a charge; it is the sweep of the cape as a bull charges.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who makes cape passes as the bull charges.

clue.text: Mass in its full version

parts.note: Mass. is the postal abbreviation of a US state, here spelt out in full

explanation.surface: A church Mass performed complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' suggests a church service or a musical setting of it, but it is the abbreviated name of a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Massachusetts is the New England state whose standard abbreviation is Mass.

clue.text: Mole that is infiltrating public relations

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so the short Latin abbreviation goes within the other piece

parts.note: i.e. (id est) is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A spy has wormed their way into a publicity department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' suggests a spy, fitting 'infiltrating', but it is the harbour sense: a stone breakwater or jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a stone breakwater or causeway at a harbour, much like a jetty projecting into the sea.

clue.text: A sign that a professional man is prepared to do business

definitions.text: A sign that a professional man is prepared to do business

parts.words: A sign that a professional man is prepared to do business
parts.note: a plaque by a doctor's or solicitor's door announcing their practice is open

explanation.surface: Some signal that a professional is ready to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A polished metal nameplate beside a door advertises a doctor's or lawyer's practice to callers.

clue.text: Yarn that's embroidered

parts.note: a 'yarn' sounds like a tall story being embellished, but it is wool thread worked into embroidery

explanation.surface: A tall tale that has been embellished in the telling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn that's embroidered' reads like an exaggerated story; literally it is the fine worsted thread used for embroidery.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewel is a thin worsted wool used for decorative embroidery stitched onto fabric.

clue.text: Annul, even in court?

parts.note: a judge can quash a verdict, and the words also suggest picking a team for a tennis court

explanation.surface: Asking whether cancelling something works even in a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: In law, a higher court may cancel a judgment by this phrase; read literally it is also arranging a team on a court.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside a ruling is the legal phrase for cancelling or voiding it.

clue.text: Patch up one's differences with Thackeray?

definitions.meaning: to settle a quarrel and become reconciled
the Victorian novelist William Thackeray's middle name

explanation.surface: Reconciling with the author of Vanity Fair after a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: William Makepeace Thackeray wrote Vanity Fair; his middle name doubles as the phrase for ending a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reconcile after a quarrel, and it is also the Victorian novelist's middle name.

clue.text: The height of architectural draughtsmanship

definitions.meaning: a drawing showing one face of a building

explanation.surface: The peak of skill in drawing buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation means height or altitude, and also an architect's drawing of a building's face.

clue.text: Space to turn round and berth

indicators.note: turning round means the word for space is read from back to front

parts.note: room means space, as in 'room to move'

explanation.surface: A harbour with enough space for a ship to swing round and dock.
explanation.definitionFit: To moor a boat is to berth it, tying it up at a quay or mooring.

clue.text: Take off a ring, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word is chosen by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a peal is a ring of bells

explanation.surface: Removing a ring from a finger, as overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off a ring' suggests removing jewellery, but the ring is of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: To peel is to take off an outer layer, such as skin from fruit.

clue.text: Kind of crossing made by Drake's ship

definitions.meaning: a pedestrian crossing with push-button lights, a British road feature
Sir Francis Drake's ship was first named this, before becoming the Golden Hind

explanation.surface: A voyage made in Sir Francis Drake's vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a pelican crossing is a light-controlled pedestrian crossing; Drake's Golden Hind set out under the name Pelican.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird gives its name to a light-controlled British road crossing and to Drake's renamed ship.

clue.text: Fit to do the job with reservations

definitions.meaning: having the training or credentials for a post
limited or hedged, as in a guarded approval

explanation.surface: A candidate is competent, though endorsed only half-heartedly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both properly trained for a role and, of praise or approval, limited by reservations.

clue.text: It's not bound to be distributed

definitions.text: It's not bound to be distributed

parts.words: It's not bound to be distributed
parts.note: 'not bound' reads as not obliged, but means unbound like a book

explanation.surface: Something that is not obliged to be handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not bound to' looks like 'not obliged to'; it means an unbound printed sheet handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a single unbound printed sheet handed out to the public.

clue.text: Small type of gem

definitions.meaning: a size of printer's type, about six and a half point

explanation.surface: Asking what kind of small gemstone it is.
explanation.walkthrough: Old printers named type sizes; emerald is a small one between nonpareil and minion.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both an old printer's small type size and a green precious stone.

clue.text: Animal disease going round English riding school

indicators.note: the disease's letters go round the abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: mange is a skin disease of animals caused by mites

explanation.surface: An illness spreading among horses at a stables.
explanation.definitionFit: A manege is an arena or school where horses and riders are trained.

clue.text: Split seen in a sexy dress?

definitions.meaning: a division or cleft, as in a split between groups
a low-cut neckline shows the hollow between the breasts

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a split is visible in a revealing frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' suggests a torn seam; the second sense is the hollow a low neckline reveals.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a division or split, and also the hollow between breasts shown by a low neckline.

clue.text: A charming thing to wear

parts.note: 'charming' reads as delightful but means bearing a charm against evil

explanation.surface: A delightful piece of clothing or jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn as protection against evil or bad luck.

clue.text: There's a lot of interest taken in it

definitions.text: There's a lot of interest taken in it

parts.words: There's a lot of interest taken in it
parts.note: 'interest' reads as curiosity, but means money charged on a loan

explanation.surface: Something that many people find fascinating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' suggests enthusiasm; here it is the charge on a loan, taken at an exorbitant rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Usury is lending money at excessive rates of interest.

clue.text: Cacti lend a different look to a flat, perhaps

indicators.note: giving letters a different look means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Succulent plants brighten up somebody's apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' suggests a home, which the cacti brighten; in music it is a sign altering a note. 'different look' rearranges CACTI LEND A.
explanation.definitionFit: In music an accidental is a sign such as a flat or sharp altering a note's pitch.

clue.text: State without a health centre

indicators.note: the letters sit in the centre of the words that follow 'State', inside the run

explanation.surface: A US state lacking any medical clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but it is part of the hiding run: the letters come from witho-UT A H-ealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty states of the USA, with Salt Lake City as its capital.

clue.text: Ann set out for French town

indicators.note: 'out' means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman named Ann sets off on a trip to France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ANN SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a city in western France on the River Loire.

clue.text: Kept going, having support

definitions.meaning: propped by stays, the ropes or struts that brace a mast or structure

explanation.surface: Someone carried on because others backed them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means persisted or endured, and also braced by stays, the ropes or props supporting a mast.
